answer: Willow–Copper Mirror Probe: admission samples each new agent’s packet inter-arrival spectrum and clock-skew residual against a willow-shaped jitter template, then cross-correlates it with existing identities via a copper-path RTT mirror. Independent agents show uncorrelated residuals; sybils sharing a host/scheduler/clock produce matching mirror peaks. To pass, an attacker must provision separate clocks, NICs, and traffic shapers per identity and sustain realistic jitter, multiplying infrastructure and monitoring cost.
